jobs.title: Director, Chapter Lead, Media Analytics
jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

The Marketing and Client Solutions Decision Sciences ( Growth) team is at the center of our Media practice, strategy and innovation at CIBC. Its sole focus is to efficiently drive growth in reach and conversions through efficient media investments that are data driven. We work across different enterprise teams at CIBC and Simplii helping them understand and serve our clients and Canadians better each day. We apply best practices in marketing measurement, descriptive and predictive analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence and leverage the latest in big data technology platforms.

Reporting into the COE Lead for Marketing and Client solutions within AI Data and Analytics, this role is responsible for leading a Media decision sciences practice, delivering on strategic priorities, managing and maintaining team operations and senior stakeholder relationships, equipping the Media Ops teams with high quality and timely data and insights to continuously optimize our Media. This Director will lead, manage and mentor a small team of Junior and Media scientists. This role requires a hands-on approach to solving problems, planning and managing change related to all aspects of marketing sciences delivery.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Champion media analytics as a strategic growth driver — Serve as the trusted analytics partner to marketing, retail, wealth, and distribution leaders by translating business priorities into clear media measurement, experimentation, and optimization strategies. Ensure solutions are practical, scalable, and aligned to business outcomes.
Lead measurement, experimentation, and optimization across the media ecosystem — Oversee the design, implementation, and ongoing evaluation of analytics frameworks, models, and test-and-learn programs that improve media effectiveness. Guide the team in applying advanced analytics, AI/ML, and emerging GenAI capabilities to both structured and unstructured data, with a strong focus on campaign performance, attribution, audience insights, and investment optimization.
Deliver end-to-end analytical solutions — Lead work from problem definition and methodology through execution, validation, monitoring, and refinement. Continuously evolve approaches as business needs shift, new channels emerge, or performance insights suggest optimization opportunities.
Build a high-performing analytics function — Lead, coach, and develop a strong team of media analytics professionals. Hire and nurture talent with the right blend of analytical rigor, business acumen, and media expertise. Set clear expectations, remove barriers, and ensure the team is aligned to business priorities and enterprise goals.
Embed responsible, effective analytics practices — Foster high standards in measurement design, data quality, experimentation discipline, and responsible AI use. Ensure the team’s work adheres to relevant policies, governance standards, and best practices while maintaining credibility with partners across the organization.

Who You Are

You are a media analytics leader first. You bring strong command of the media landscape and understand how to connect channels, audiences, and investments to measurable business outcomes. You are fluent in media effectiveness, incrementality, attribution, testing, and optimization.
You combine craft expertise with strategic thinking. You know how to move from business question to analytical approach to actionable recommendation. You are comfortable shaping measurement strategies that inform planning, improve performance, and support better investment decisions.
You are highly analytical and experimentally minded. You have deep experience applying advanced analytics to marketing and media use cases, including forecasting, audience analysis, causal measurement, optimization, and performance diagnostics. You understand how to structure rigorous experiments and use evidence to guide decisions.
You are digitally and technically fluent. You are comfortable working with modern analytics and data science tools such as Python, SQL, Pandas, scikit-learn, and cloud-based data environments. You can partner effectively with technical teams while staying focused on business relevance and usability.
You are an effective translator between technical and business teams. You can turn complex analytical concepts into clear, compelling narratives for senior stakeholders. You know how to influence decisions, build trust, and bring partners along in environments with complexity and ambiguity.
You are a strong people leader. You lead with clarity, accountability, and empathy. You develop talent, elevate team capability, and create an inclusive environment where high performance and collaboration go hand in hand.
You understand applied AI in a marketing context.— You have experience using traditional AI/ML techniques and an appreciation for where GenAI can enhance workflows, insight generation, and decision support. You are thoughtful about where these tools add value and where rigor in measurement must remain paramount.
You bring strong business and industry judgment. Experience in marketing, media, or sales analytics is essential, and financial services experience is a strong asset. You understand how to operate in a regulated, complex environment while still driving innovation and impact.
You are well-credentialed and credible. You bring advanced academic training in analytics, statistics, economics, mathematics, computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, along with a track record of delivering large, high-impact analytical initiatives.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.
We cultivate a culture where you can express your ambition through initiatives like Purpose Day; a paid day off dedicated for you to use to invest in your growth and development.
Subject to plan and program terms and conditions

What You Need To Know

CIBC is committed to creating an inclusive environment where all team members and clients feel like they belong. We seek applicants with a wide range of abilities and we provide an accessible candidate experience. If you need accommodation, please contact Mailbox.careers-carrieres@cibc.com
CIBC is committed to clarity in our hiring process. All roles posted are opportunities we’re actively recruiting for, unless stated otherwise.
You need to be legally eligible to work at the location(s) specified above and, where applicable, must have a valid work or study permit.
We may ask you to complete an attribute-based assessment and other skills test (such as simulation, coding, French proficiency).
We use artificial intelligence tools during the recruitment process. Our goal for the application process is to get to know more about you, all that you have to offer, and give you the opportunity to learn more about us.

jobs.title: Director, Corporate Risk Information Management
jobs.description:
You are as unique as your background, experience and point of view. Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered and challenged to be your best self. You'll work with dynamic colleagues - experts in their fields - who are eager to share their knowledge with you. Your leaders will inspire and help you reach your potential and soar to new heights. Every day, you'll have new and exciting opportunities to make life brighter for our Clients - who are at the heart of everything we do.

At Sun Life, we're driven by our Purpose: helping our Clients achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. Our values shape how we work: caring, authentic, bold, inspiring, and impactful.

When you join Sun Life, you'll work with passionate colleagues and empowering leaders who support your growth and celebrate your contributions, so you can make a meaningful difference in our Clients' lives.

Discover how you can make a difference in the lives of individuals, families and communities around the world.

Job Description:

About The Role

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President, Emerging Risk Management & Strategic Risk Initiatives, the Director, Corporate Risk Information Management is accountable for the oversight of the information management, records management, and data governance policy requirements and underlying programs across Corporate Risk, which includes Enterprise & Operational Risk Management, Insurance & Financial Risk Management, Investment & Credit Risk Management, and the Corporate and DBTS Business Group Risk Office teams. The Director sets direction, maintains the framework and methodology, and holds Information Stewards, Records Officers, Records Custodians, Data Custodians and Risk Office teams accountable so that information assets are properly classified, protected, retained, disposed of, and governed in alignment with the Enterprise Information Management Policy, regulatory expectations, and business needs. The Director leads continuous improvement of the program, including enhancements to tools, and strengthens program governance, effectiveness, and efficiency.

The Director is the accountable owner for structured and non-structured business records and information assets within Corporate Risk, in line with the Enterprise Information Management Policy.

The role holds the Records Steward, Records Officer, Data Governance Operational Lead, and Non-Structured Data Information Stewardship accountabilities for Corporate Risk, reflecting the centralized operating model of the function. It provides integrated oversight of information lifecycle management, repository governance, data quality, metadata, reporting, and information risk management, and ensures consistent execution of records and information management requirements across Corporate Risk.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead information governance, risk, and compliance

Serve as the accountable lead for Non-Structured Information Management governance for Corporate Risk.
Maintain the Corporate Risk information management framework, operating guidelines, and standards, aligned to the Enterprise Information Management Policy, and oversee adherence to policy and related control expectations.
Provide guidance and advice to Business Group Risk Office teams and business leaders when judgement or clarification is required on information governance obligations, risks, and implementation requirements. Provide advice into strategic decisions and program improvements.
On a quarterly basis, independently evaluate the Corporate Risk information management risk profile, including Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), and report results, material non-compliance, and significant issues to senior management and the Operational Risk and Compliance Committee (ORCC) in a timely manner.
Oversee and coordinate Corporate Risk's response to Risk Control Self Assessments, audits, compliance reviews, and regulatory examinations, and oversee related issue remediation activities related to information management.
Prepare an annual report to senior management and ORCC on the status of the information management, records management, and data governance program.
Establish, maintain, and continually enhance the oversight and monitoring frameworks for the program.
Monitor and benchmark Corporate Risk information management practices against industry standards, regulatory expectations, and best practices, and assess complex information risk issues to guide solution recommendations.
Develop and own the short- and mid-term strategy and roadmap for information management, records management, and data governance in Corporate Risk, aligned to enterprise and Business Group strategy, and provide significant input to Corporate Risk's strategic and long-term plans.
Set program roll out objectives and plan and prioritize program resources, milestones, and dependencies across Corporate Risk.

Records and information lifecycle management

Direct and oversee records management activities, including records classification, retention, legal holds, disposition, and remediation planning.
Perform and oversee Records Officer responsibilities for Corporate Risk, retaining accountability for consistent execution of records management requirements, guidance, monitoring, and issue follow-up.
Oversee Records Impact Assessments (RIAs) and Records Management Risk Reviews when new or changed processes, systems, repositories, vendors, or operating models may affect the creation, storage, access, retention, transfer, or disposition of Corporate Risk business records, and provide guidance on complex or high-risk cases.
Oversee the maintenance of records and repository inventories and ensure ownership and stewardship assignments remain current.
Determine how Corporate Risk business records are identified, classified, captured, stored, protected, retained, and disposed of, and hold Records Custodians accountable for applying those determinations.
Make final decisions within Corporate Risk on record designation, retention and disposition, legal hold implementation, and exceptions to records requirements, and escalate only matters that require enterprise policy interpretation or an exception to enterprise policy.

Advance data governance and repository oversight

Provide oversight and approval of Data Governance artifacts and Business Impact Statements prepared by Information Stewards.
Lead data quality, metadata, business glossary, lineage, classification, and critical information inventory practices, including the related standards and methodology.
Monitor and report Data Governance KPIs and oversee remediation of identified issues.
Lead governance of SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other non-structured business repositories.

Enable change and stakeholder engagement

Build strong working relationships with Information Owners, Records Custodians, Information Custodians, Risk Offices, Compliance, Legal, Technology, Data Governance teams, and other relevant teams involved in records and data management to drive execution of key deliverables within the Three Lines of Defense model.
Develop, maintain, and deliver training, communications, and practical guidance to Information Stewards, Records Custodians, Risk Office teams, and other stakeholders to support adoption of information governance practices.
Lead cross-functional discussions to resolve issues, mature governance practices, and embed sustainable ways of working.
Represent Corporate Risk on peer Steering Groups and provide direction on information management matters.
Work closely with Business Group Risk Office teams on the effective roll-out of program changes.
Develop and communicate the vision for information governance in Corporate Risk and build consensus on operating goals aligned with the Risk division.

What You'll Need To Succeed

University degree in Information Management, Data Governance, Records Management, Business Administration, Risk Management, Library Sciences, Information Technology, or a related discipline, and/or relevant certification.
5+ years of risk management, records management, data governance, or information governance experience, with a proven track record of designing and implementing effective programs, controls, and processes, ideally within a major federally regulated financial institution.
Direct experience writing policies and guidelines, and implementing governance frameworks, standards, controls, or enterprise operating procedures.
Demonstrable experience leading cross-functional initiatives, developing strong working relationships, and influencing senior stakeholders in a large, matrixed organization within the Three Lines of Defense model.
Proven experience dealing with complexity and ambiguity, using broad knowledge, keen analysis, and sound professional judgement to arrive at quality decisions.
Working knowledge of Sunlife’s information management, records management, data governance, privacy, compliance, and operational risk practices.
Ability to translate complex policy, risk, records, and data governance requirements into clear business guidance, communications, training, and sustainable operating practices.Strong knowledge of information management, records management, and data governance principles, including information lifecycle management, repository governance, metadata management, information classification, and data quality management, with the ability to assess, measure, and monitor information risk.
Strong knowledge of the information and records management landscape, financial industry leading practices, and regulator expectations.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities, with keen attention to detail, and experience in risk assessment, control design, compliance monitoring, reporting, and analytics.
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, shared mailboxes, network drives, and other collaboration platforms.
Experience implementing, managing, and maintaining a records, information governance, or GRC tool.
Strategic mindset, with the ability to understand business requirements and develop innovative solutions.
Excellent communication, facilitation, influencing, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate complex concepts to a diverse audience.
Well-developed writing and visual presentation skills to articulate analytic results, options, recommendations, and reporting.
Effective change management and change leadership through impact and influence skills, with governance oversight and a continuous improvement mindset.
Proactive and adaptable mindset, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced and rapidly evolving organization.

What's in it for you:

Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives.
In 2024, Sun Life ranked among the top 100 most sustainable global corporations by Corporate Knights for the 15th consecutive year, leading Canadian insurers.
We are proud to be on the 2024 Best Workplaces in Canada list by Great Place to Work.
We’re also listed as one of the Best Workplaces for Women and Best Workplaces with Most Trusted Executive Teams.
Our unique Sabbatical Program gives you the opportunity to take up to 6 weeks off, every five years.
Care Days available for self-care or care of others (i.e., family or others you may support) and Sick Days to support your well-being.

The Base Pay range is for the primary location for which the job is posted. It may vary depending on the work location of the successful candidate or other factors. In addition to Base Pay, eligible Sun Life employees participate in various incentive plans, payment under which is discretionary and subject to individual and company performance. Certain sales focused roles have sales incentive plans based on individual or group sales results.

jobs.description:
Permanent

Department: FSD Client Management (520)

30 Adelaide Str, East

Who We Are

With its global headquarters in Toronto, Canada, International Financial Data Services (IFDS) is a world-leading provider of outsourcing and technology solutions to the financial services industry. IFDS services over 240 financial organizations around the world, providing solutions to a wide range of global asset managers, wealth managers, banks, and insurance companies. The IFDS enterprise supports more than 17 million accounts with AUA of approximately CAD $4 trillion. IFDS Canada is a 50/50 joint ventures between Boston-based State Street Corporation, one of the world’s leading providers of financial services to institutional investors, and Connecticut-based SS&C Technologies, a global provider of investment and financial software-enabled services and software for the global financial services and healthcare industries.

Imagine yourself at IFDS

Come experience a community like no other at International Financial Data Services (IFDS). We offer work opportunities driven by a passion for creating market leading financial solutions, and a culture that nurtures collaboration, accountability, diversity & inclusion, and continuous learning. We’ll provide you with opportunities to develop your career. From ongoing training and development programs to experiences working with our global financial services partners, you’ll be able to realize your full potential.

Role Overview

The Governance Director – Client Account Management provides day to day oversight; guidance and strategic leadership to our client and the broader support team at IFDS and SS&C through close collaboration with the Business Development Relationship Manager, the AMS team, IT Departments; the Business Solutions and Planning team and C-Suite individuals to ensure the delivery of superior service commitments aligned with client goals. The incumbent will own the overall oversight of key initiatives and changes impacting the client, identifying risks and issues and will be responsible for the timely closure of all remediation actions. The Director will provide guidance and leadership, coaching and development to managers and employees to ensure that clients are supported with high quality solutions tailored to their business needs.

Governance

Role Responsibilities

Oversee a virtual support team consisting of both IFDS and SS&C individuals dedicated to the overall successful delivery of changes.
Build and maintain a governance practice consisting of key reporting and metrics tracking all initiatives/changes / issues - identifying and addressing risks and issues to continuously enhance service, client relationships and improve operational efficiencies.
Acts as an escalation point for the client re any key changes.
Lead the identification and documentation of risks and controls across changes and initiatives (projects, service requests, incidents and adhoc initiatives such as proactive testing of complex functionality).
Elevate the profile and product knowledge of clients by providing deep expertise in risk and controls in conjunction with virtual support team.
Implement an internal/ external forum/s to meet regularly with the “virtual” support teams (and the client) to provide and discuss status of changes/issues and hold teams accountable to timely resolution and remediation actions.
Ongoing assessment of venues / documentation and ensures all processes serve a key purpose and align with client and IFDS requirements. E.g. any “special client reporting” from CAMs – Vendor Scorecard; Usage reporting; Utilization reporting etc. Delivers to client (along with new findings/solutions etc)
Ongoing review processes/operating model etc. to ensure “we evolve our processes and engagement” aligned with iA’s evolution in business growth and strategy
Overseas the SLA adherence and smooth delivery of client requests, to ensure delivery is in accordance with client expectations
Work directly with the client and internal teams to ensure clarity and organization of all changes and release/ delivery dates.
Develop and maintain strong relationships with stakeholders, business partners to ensure effective collaboration and communication.
Drive change management initiatives, guiding the team through evolving operational risk management standards and expectations.
Foster a team environment and culture that encourages productivity, innovation, process improvement, and professionalism.

Account Management Service Delivery

Oversees day-to-day issue resolution and all critical reoccurring processes for clients, which includes planning and execution of the overall client service delivery experience in collaboration with all internal and external clients to oversee the delivery of superior customer service in alignment with the client’s strategic goals 
Interacts directly with key business partners, developing and maintaining a strong on-going relationship; always looking for opportunities to improve client satisfaction and experience
Facilitates and leads various internal / client meetings (virtually and / or in person) as it relates to the mandate and participates in all key reoccurring meetings regarding TLR; Release Management; JAD sessions; client reviews
Oversees the various aspects of client business operations, regulatory, statutory and industry standards bodies to understand and ensure appropriate and timely communication of business requirements for client consumption in collaboration with internal and external teams
Acts as an escalation point for Client Account Managers on incidents/service requests and the client if resolution is not attained timely / accurately
Supports Business Development & Relationship Management with new product onboarding opportunities as required.

Leadership and People Management

Completes performance reviews; successions plans; establishing objectives in monitoring performance against plans; promotes training and professional development. Works closely with Human Resources on talent management
Provides performance feedback, coaching, mentoring and career and development planning for team members
Ensures continued employee engagement by promoting an “in the office presence” through participation in IFDS events; team meetings and events; internal working groups
Reviews current operating procedures, revising and implementing changes to improve service levels, productivity and cost effectiveness
Maintains current knowledge of financial; regulatory and operational issues affecting other departments and the company as a whole. Understands financial and operational goals of IFDS
Provides the team with support and recommendations on project prioritization and resource management
Oversees and provides the team guidance and direction with new opportunities with the development and discussion of operational enhancements to improve the client experience which may include but not limited to guidance with approach; test strategy and developing test plan and cases
Oversees and provides the team guidance and direction with new processes, policies and special initiatives as needed to enhance and support business needs.
Assists VP Account Management with salary administration; capacity planning and staffing plans

Minimum Qualifications

Demonstrated superior leadership skills including collaboration; relationship building; coaching; integrity; resilience to a fast paced; high stress environment; ownership and accountability, credibility, and consensus building
Demonstrated proficiency in communicating complex business solutions with clients & internal stakeholders
Solid technical knowledge of IFDS applications (including iFast, IFWP, etc).

jobs.title: Financial Director
jobs.description:
The Company

Our client is a global and growth-focused organization seeking an experienced Director of Finance to lead and develop the finance function for a new Canadian business unit. This is a key executive leadership position offering the opportunity to influence strategic direction, strengthen financial performance, and support continued business growth through sound financial management and business partnering.

The Role

Reporting to senior executive leadership, the Director of Finance is responsible for the overall strategic, operational, and leadership oversight of the Finance function. The role ensures strong financial governance, reporting accuracy, compliance, and financial decision support across the organization.

As a trusted advisor to executive management, Group Finance, and key business stakeholders, you will build a scalable and high-performing finance organization that drives transparency, operational excellence, value creation, and sustainable growth.
You must be comfortable leading a new Finance team in a startup environment. You will help create financial processes, internal controls and financial reporting from the ground up. This role is best suited to someone who can effectively operate in chaotic environments with the goal of creating a world class manufacturing facility.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy

Develop and execute the company's finance strategy in alignment with overall business objectives.
Provide strategic financial leadership and support executive decision-making.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and multi-year business plans.
Define, monitor, and report on key financial and operational performance indicators.
Drive financial performance reviews and support data-driven business decisions.

Financial Management & Reporting

Oversee all financial reporting activities, ensuring timely and accurate weekly, monthly, and annual reporting.
Maintain full responsibility for profit and loss management, balance sheet integrity, cash flow, and financial KPIs.
Ensure robust financial controls, governance frameworks, and compliance with accounting standards and company policies.
Manage relationships with external auditors, banks, insurers, and other financial stakeholders.

Business Partnering & Performance Optimization

Partner closely with Operations, Commercial, Supply Chain, and People & Culture leaders to improve business performance.
Identify and drive cost optimization, efficiency improvements, and profitability initiatives across the organization.
Support investment decisions through financial modelling, business cases, and risk assessments.
Promote a strong performance-oriented and data-driven culture.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, coach, and develop the Finance team to ensure high levels of performance, engagement, and accountability.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, processes, and decision-making frameworks.
Foster collaboration and continuous capability development within the finance function.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

Strengthen internal controls, risk management practices, and financial compliance.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on reporting processes, systems, tools, and ways of working.
Ensure lessons learned, root cause analysis, and performance reviews support organizational learning and continuous development.

Your Profile

Significant leadership experience within finance, ideally in manufacturing, food production, or CPG industry.
Proven track record of leading finance functions and delivering business performance improvements.
Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, strategic planning, and financial performance management.
Sound understanding of governance, compliance, financial controls, and risk management.
Experience supporting operational leadership teams in a fast-paced business environment.
Knowledge of ERP and Business Intelligence platforms, ideally SAP and related reporting tools.
Strong analytical and commercial acumen with a data-driven approach to decision-making.
Executive presence and perfect communication skills as this individual will be client-facing and regularly meet with Senior Leadership in Canada and at Head Office in Europe.
10+ years of experience including minimum 5 years as Controller.
CPA designation or MBA is required.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic, structured, and results-oriented leader.
High integrity with a strong ethical and professional approach.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Strong business acumen with the ability to influence at executive level.
Resilient and adaptable, with the ability to manage complexity and change.
Passionate about developing people and building high-performing teams.
Collaborative, hands-on, and focused on delivering practical business outcomes.

What's on Offer

This is a unique opportunity to join a growing organization in a highly visible leadership role. You will have the chance to shape the financial direction of the business, influence strategic decisions, and lead a talented finance team while contributing to the company's long-term success and growth.

jobs.title: Regional Vice President RVP Equipment Finance Sales
jobs.description:
A career as a Regional Vice-President (RVP), Equipment Finance Sales, Western Canada at National Bank is an opportunity to lead the regional Vendor Sales and Direct Sales channels as one coordinated sales organization. 
In this role, you will establish and execute the regional growth strategy, strengthen relationships with equipment vendors and business clients, and lead teams accountable for profitable origination, client acquisition and portfolio development. 
You will work closely with Commercial Banking & 1859 and Equipment Finance partners to deliver sound financing solutions while managing credit, operational and regulatory risk within the Bank's established frameworks.

Your role:

Define and execute an integrated regional strategy for Vendor Sales and Direct Sales, translating business priorities into clear market coverage, growth plans and performance expectations.
Lead the achievement of regional revenue, volume, profitability, client acquisition, vendor relationship and referral objectives across both sales channels.
Guide leaders and sales professionals in developing new business, deepening vendor and client relationships, and building a balanced pipeline across equipment sectors, client segments and geographic markets.
Create clear accountability through business plans, budgets, forecasts, activity measures and performance reporting, and take timely action when results or market conditions require adjustment.
Promote disciplined pricing and deal structuring, balancing growth, client value and return expectations within delegated authorities and established approval processes.
Maintain a strong market presence by being active in the field with clients, vendors, centres of influence and regional partners, while working closely with other market leaders to identify growth opportunities, strengthen referral networks and represent Equipment Finance consistently across the assigned region.
Work in partnership with Credit, Operations, Risk and other internal specialists to support efficient execution, appropriate risk management and a consistent client and partner experience from origination through funding.
Strengthen collaboration between Vendor Sales, Direct Sales and Commercial Banking by developing referral routines, clarifying accountabilities and connecting clients to broader Bank capabilities when appropriate.
Build and maintain senior relationships with important vendors, clients, centres of influence and industry stakeholders, and represent National Bank Equipment Finance in the regional marketplace.
Lead, coach and develop regional sales leaders and team members, establishing a high-performance, inclusive and accountable culture focused on client outcomes, collaboration and sustainable growth.
Lead change initiatives affecting the regional sales model, including process, technology, coverage, talent and operating-model improvements.
Manage the region's sales resources and expenses within approved budgets and ensure adherence to Bank policies, conduct expectations, compliance requirements and risk controls.

Your team:

You are part of the Equipment Finance and Commercial Banking leadership network and collaborate closely with colleagues in Credit, Operations, Risk, Product, Finance, Human Resources and other specialized groups. The role provides leadership across the Vendor Sales and Direct Sales teams in its assigned region.
This role can be based in either Edmonton, Calgary, Vancouver or Winnipeg.

Required skills:

Bachelor's degree in business, finance, commerce or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and senior leadership experience.
Extensive experience in commercial sales, business development and people leadership within equipment finance, commercial lending, leasing or a related financial services environment.
Demonstrated ability to lead multiple sales channels or teams and translate strategy into measurable regional results.
Strong knowledge of commercial credit, equipment finance structures, pricing, portfolio economics and risk-management expectations.
Previous experience in Equipment Finance, including direct exposure to equipment lending, leasing, vendor programs or related financing structures.
Proven ability to build senior relationships, negotiate complex opportunities and influence across business lines and functional teams.
Experience establishing sales plans, budgets, forecasts, performance measures and accountability routines.
Strong leadership, coaching, talent-development and change-management capabilities.
Proven ability to motivate and lead high-performing teams, develop talent and build leadership capability through coaching, feedback and clear performance expectations.

jobs.title: Director of Digital Marketing (Remote, Vancouver)
jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Role Vision and Impact

The Senior Director, Information Security and End-User Technology, serves as CBC/Radio-Canada’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). A strategic, visionary and collaborative leader, the CISO defines, implements and drives the overarching vision for cybersecurity, risk management and technological resilience across all corporate environments.

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations.
The Senior Director optimally balances rigorous security architecture governance with the flexibility that creative, journalistic and technical teams need to innovate and broadcast without disruption.

Operating at a senior executive level, the CISO regularly briefs and advises the Board of Directors (BoD),
the Audit Committee,
the CBC/Radio-Canada Senior Executive Team (SET)
and the T&I Management Executive Team (MET).

Supported by a team of experienced directors and senior managers overseeing governance, security operations, end-user technology and identity management, the Senior Director serves as the cornerstone of digital trust and strategic transformation for Canada’s public broadcaster.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Vision, Leadership and Executive Relations

Develop, champion and execute an enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy aligned with the Corporation’s business mission, risk profile and digital transformation.
Serve as a trusted expert and strategic adviser to the BoD, Audit Committee, SET and MET regarding risk status, security posture and maturity, and required investments.
Foster a “Security by Design” culture and establish security architecture governance frameworks that keep operational and production workflows running smoothly while proactively managing risk.
Anticipate technology trends and lead the secure integration of artificial intelligence (AI/GenAI) and automation into business processes and security defences across the organization.

Securing IT, Cloud, Distribution and Broadcast/Operational Technology (OT) Environments

Define and continuously adapt the security strategy across the entire technology landscape, including corporate IT infrastructure, cloud systems, end-user environments, and critical production, broadcast and network infrastructure.
Ensure the resilience of content acquisition, processing and distribution workflows against threats targeting the media sector and critical infrastructure.

Governance, Risk, Compliance and AI Governance

Oversee the governance function responsible for developing, maintaining and enforcing policies, standards, security architecture principles, exception management and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, AI frameworks).
Lead the third-party and partner risk management program (covering vendors and technology contracts) in close collaboration with the Legal Services and Procurement teams.
Co-develop a governance, compliance and ethical framework for the enterprise-wide use of AI and generative AI, assessing specific risks throughout their life cycle.
Ensure strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., Quebec’s Law 25, GDPR and sector-specific requirements).
Drive a cybersecurity culture and awareness program focused on lasting behaviour change across the organization.

Defence Operations, SOC and Crisis Management

Oversee the performance and modernization of the Security Operations Centre (SOC), advanced detection tools (SIEM, EDR/XDR, automation) and continuous threat monitoring.
Direct major security incident response operations and lead technology crisis management, from detection to full business recovery.
Oversee regular penetration testing, vulnerability assessments and cyberattack simulation exercises across IT, broadcast and distribution environments.

Identity and End-User Technology

Guide the strategic vision for Identity and Access Management (IAM, PAM) to provide secure, simple and frictionless access for all staff and contractors.
Collaborate closely with the End-User Technology teams to align security with a modern, efficient and intuitive employee experience.

Financial Management and Team Engagement

Plan and optimize the cybersecurity department’s overall budget and partner with internal procurement teams to negotiate major technology contracts.
Inspire, coach and develop a team of directors and senior managers — fostering excellence, innovation and cross-functional collaboration.
Lead with the heart.

Qualifications, Experience And Core Competencies

Education and Certifications

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, cybersecurity, computer engineering, business administration (IT concentration) or a related field.
At least one recognized executive-level professional certification: CISSP, CISM, CCISO, CISA or CRISC.

Professional Experience

Seven to 10 years of experience managing professional teams or equivalent.
Deep expertise in technology architecture, cloud security, network infrastructure, cryptography, and identity and access management (IAM).
Ability to provide collaborative leadership within the organization to see complex, transformational initiatives through to completion.
Demonstrated skills in planning, organizing and engaging teams.
Proven ability and track record in leading cross-functional teams.
Proven ability to work with cross-functional, agile teams or on projects that have multi-team dependencies.
Ability to distil complex issues into clear, concise presentations and reports.
Expertise in the various technologies typically used by journalists in a newsroom.
Knowledge of business practices, including drafting plans and specifications, contracts, negotiation, finance, and IT management software.
Knowledge of software development and the technology infrastructure required for product delivery.
Knowledge of workflows for content acquisition, management and distribution, with a focus on storytelling.
Innovative approach to technical and operational challenges, paired with sound judgment to protect CBC/Radio-Canada from legal liability and financial loss.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with an ability to engage and influence stakeholders and partners at every level of the organization.
Excellent ability to listen to and communicate with people having different points of view or competing business objectives.
Experience implementing product governance models.
Ability to travel occasionally between Montreal and Toronto.
Bilingualism (English and French), both spoken and written.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Software Engineering - Contract Intelligence
jobs.description:
This is a fully remote opportunity.

As the most trusted global leader in data-first contract lifecycle management (CLM) software, Agiloft helps organizations manage the end-to-end process of proposing, negotiating, signing, and leveraging contracts using our flexible Data-first Agreement Platform (DAP). With contract data as the foundation, customers quickly and collaboratively reach agreement and leverage contract visibility to thrive with competitive advantage. Employing powerful, pragmatic artificial intelligence as a legal force multiplier, and robust integration capabilities as a data liberator, organizations around the world trust Agiloft’s certified implementers to deliver connected, intelligent, and autonomous solutions across the entire contract lifecycle.

Top analysts like Gartner, Forrester, and IDC agree, all showing Agiloft as a leader in the CLM space. Our no code platform is easily managed and administered by business users, which is why Agiloft is the contract you keep: nearly a full 100% of new customers are satisfied with their initial implementations, and some 97% of customers renew every year. Ours is a growing, vibrant, successful company that is at the forefront of a market that is becoming a must-have for all organizations.

We believe that the way to build the strongest, most vibrant place to work is to bring in individuals from all walks of life, and to support them in bringing their authentic selves to their day, every day. Our working philosophy is that “EX = CX”: when employee experience is excellent, so is customer experience. We support multiple Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), and offer a working environment that supports healthy work/life balance, including floating holidays and a quarterly, no-questions-asked wellness day.

Position Overview

AI is changing CLM, and Agiloft is building what comes next. As Senior Director, Software Engineering - Contract Intelligence, you will lead the engineering teams behind Astra Agents and the Contract Intelligence Graph (CIG). These are the capabilities that turn contracts into intelligence customers act on every day. You will own engineering strategy, organization, and execution across this portfolio, together with the shared platform components and interfaces that serve these experiences.

This is a rare chance to shape and build a converged platform that makes these products work as one and that future Agiloft experiences will build on. The shared platform scope includes common data models and database services, identity and access management (IAM), agent and AI Assistant capabilities, and a unified interface suite spanning APIs, user interfaces, and MCP servers. You will decide how each product consumes these capabilities while preserving the flexibility each experience needs.

Reporting directly to the CTO and working closely with Product, Design, Applied AI & Knowledge Engineering, Core CLM Engineering, and Cloud Operations, you will turn ambitious product priorities into an integrated technical roadmap and dependable delivery that drives measurable customer value.

You will lead managers, technical leaders, and distributed teams. This role is for a leader who stays close to the code, holds a high bar, and builds a culture where strong engineers do their best work.
Success means shared capabilities are adopted across Astra and CLM, the architecture remains secure and scalable, releases are predictable, and the organization can deliver customer value without sacrificing quality, reliability, or long-term maintainability. If you want to shape how enterprises manage their contracts in the AI era, and build the team that makes it happen, we’d love to talk with you.

Job Responsibilities

Contract Intelligence Strategy & Outcomes

Own engineering outcomes across Astra and the CLM cloud-native services for Agents and CIG, including the APIs, integrations, and orchestration capabilities that support them.
Partner with Product and Design leadership to shape strategy, roadmap, sequencing, and investment decisions, using customer feedback and adoption signals to guide priorities.
Translate portfolio priorities into integrated engineering plans, technical investments, clear ownership, and explicit cross-team dependencies.
Define and review measures of customer impact, adoption, business value, delivery predictability, and product quality.

Converged Platform Architecture & Interfaces

Define architecture direction and a convergence roadmap for shared data models, database services, IAM, Agents, and AI Assistants serving Astra and CLM cloud-native services for Agents and CIG.
Design shared components so they can be consumed consistently across Astra and CLM while allowing product-specific extensions where needed; establish clear service boundaries and ownership across Astra, Agents, CIG, and Core CLM.
Own a unified interface suite across APIs, user interfaces, and MCP servers, with consistent contracts and patterns for Astra and CLM cloud-native Agent and CIG services.
Guide cloud-native APIs and integrations, including MCP and other AI orchestration interfaces for Contract Intelligence workflows and customer systems; ensure services are secure, tenant-aware, scalable, observable, versioned, reliable, and backward compatible.
Improve API, UI, and MCP design standards, documentation, and developer experience for Agiloft teams, customers, and partners.

Agents, AI Assistants & Contract Intelligence Graph

Partner with Applied AI & Knowledge Engineering to translate AI and knowledge capabilities into production-ready Agents and AI Assistants, service interfaces, architecture, and engineering plans.
Establish practices for evaluating AI-enabled features, including output quality, permissions, privacy, latency, cost, and operational behavior.
Guide engineering evolution of CIG and the services used by Agents and AI Assistants so they provide a dependable foundation for Contract Intelligence experiences across Astra and CLM.
Set appropriate technical guardrails for AI-powered workflows and integrations with external systems.

Delivery Excellence & Operational Reliability

Own the software development lifecycle across the Contract Intelligence engineering organization, including planning, development, testing, release coordination, and post-release stabilization.
Coordinate dependencies and release plans across Astra, CLM cloud-native services, Core CLM, and other integration teams.
Establish operational measures such as service availability, API latency, error rates, integration reliability, and incident recurrence; use them to drive improvement.
Lead root-cause analysis and remediation for significant incidents and Level 3 technical escalations within the domain.
Balance roadmap delivery with reliability, security, modernization, performance, and long-term technical health.
Be a hands-on technical contributor to the codebase, code reviews, and architecture decisions.

Organization, Talent & Cross-functional Leadership

Lead managers and technical leaders responsible for Astra, Agents, CIG, and the supporting integration capabilities.
Align Astra team priorities and technical direction with shared components and CLM cloud-native services while maintaining clear accountability for each product outcome.
Develop managers and senior engineers through clear expectations, coaching, delegation, feedback, performance management, and career development.
Build an accountable, collaborative engineering culture with strong technical ownership, predictable execution, and continuous learning across distributed teams.
Recruit, onboard, develop, and retain strong engineering talent; identify capability, capacity, and organizational needs as the portfolio grows.
Partner across Product, Design, Core CLM, Applied AI & Knowledge Engineering, QA, Cloud Operations, Security, and Support to resolve dependencies and deliver customer outcomes.
Communicate technical direction, tradeoffs, delivery risks, and investment needs clearly; serve as an engineering escalation point for complex Contract Intelligence issues.
Other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years of progressive software engineering experience, including 5+ years leading and developing multi-team engineering organizations with managers and senior technical leaders with clear delivery accountability and performance management.
Demonstrated ownership of engineering outcomes for a substantial product portfolio, platform, or technical domain, measured by customer adoption, usage, and business value.
Deep experience with cloud-based SaaS systems, distributed services, APIs, enterprise integrations, and user-facing applications, with sufficient technical fluency to guide architecture and evaluate tradeoffs.
Demonstrated success building shared or converged components used by multiple products or services, including data models, database services, and IAM, with clear interfaces and ownership boundaries.
Hands-on technical fluency in production AI/LLM functionality, Agents, and AI Assistants, including the engineering practices needed to assess quality, privacy, reliability, and cost.
Strong understanding of engineering measures such as delivery predictability, service reliability and SLOs, defect trends, performance, and operational health.
Proven partnership with Product and Design to turn customer priorities into executable engineering roadmaps, including sound build, buy or partner decisions, and to deliver predictability against reliability and quality measure.
Clear communicator who translates technical risks, tradeoffs and decisions into business terms for executives and cross-functional partners.
Sound responsible AI judgement, with experience setting guardrails for accuracy, privacy, security, permissions, transparency and human oversight in customer-facing AI features.
Develops managers and technical leaders, builds succession and helps people do their best work.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading AI-enabled products, Agent architectures, or orchestration interfaces such as MCP.
Experience with knowledge graphs, graph-based systems, or other data-rich enterprise platforms.
Background in CLM, legal technology, workflow automation, or enterprise SaaS.
Experience scaling engineering organizations and operating practices as products grow, including in compliance-driven environments.

Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non- overtime eligible) position.
Paid parental leave

Ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace is our priority. We are committed to an environment of acceptance where you are free to bring your full self to work. All employment decisions at Agiloft are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications without regard to race, color, religion or belief, national or social ethnic origin, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, parental status, marital status, Veteran status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. If you have a need that requires accommodation during the recruiting process, please let us know by contacting Director, Talent Acquisition, Brad Toothman at brad.toothman@agiloft.com.

Applicants from underrepresented groups such as minorities, veterans, or individuals with disabilities encouraged to apply.

new_jobs.title: Financial Director
new_jobs.description:
The Company

Our client is a global and growth-focused organization seeking an experienced Director of Finance to lead and develop the finance function for a new Canadian business unit. This is a key executive leadership position offering the opportunity to influence strategic direction, strengthen financial performance, and support continued business growth through sound financial management and business partnering.

The Role

Reporting to senior executive leadership, the Director of Finance is responsible for the overall strategic, operational, and leadership oversight of the Finance function. The role ensures strong financial governance, reporting accuracy, compliance, and financial decision support across the organization.

As a trusted advisor to executive management, Group Finance, and key business stakeholders, you will build a scalable and high-performing finance organization that drives transparency, operational excellence, value creation, and sustainable growth.
You must be comfortable leading a new Finance team in a startup environment. You will help create financial processes, internal controls and financial reporting from the ground up. This role is best suited to someone who can effectively operate in chaotic environments with the goal of creating a world class manufacturing facility.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Leadership & Strategy

Develop and execute the company's finance strategy in alignment with overall business objectives.
Provide strategic financial leadership and support executive decision-making.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and multi-year business plans.
Define, monitor, and report on key financial and operational performance indicators.
Drive financial performance reviews and support data-driven business decisions.

Financial Management & Reporting

Oversee all financial reporting activities, ensuring timely and accurate weekly, monthly, and annual reporting.
Maintain full responsibility for profit and loss management, balance sheet integrity, cash flow, and financial KPIs.
Ensure robust financial controls, governance frameworks, and compliance with accounting standards and company policies.
Manage relationships with external auditors, banks, insurers, and other financial stakeholders.

Business Partnering & Performance Optimization

Partner closely with Operations, Commercial, Supply Chain, and People & Culture leaders to improve business performance.
Identify and drive cost optimization, efficiency improvements, and profitability initiatives across the organization.
Support investment decisions through financial modelling, business cases, and risk assessments.
Promote a strong performance-oriented and data-driven culture.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, coach, and develop the Finance team to ensure high levels of performance, engagement, and accountability.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, processes, and decision-making frameworks.
Foster collaboration and continuous capability development within the finance function.

Governance & Continuous Improvement

Strengthen internal controls, risk management practices, and financial compliance.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on reporting processes, systems, tools, and ways of working.
Ensure lessons learned, root cause analysis, and performance reviews support organizational learning and continuous development.

Your Profile

Significant leadership experience within finance, ideally in manufacturing, food production, or CPG industry.
Proven track record of leading finance functions and delivering business performance improvements.
Strong experience with budgeting, forecasting, strategic planning, and financial performance management.
Sound understanding of governance, compliance, financial controls, and risk management.
Experience supporting operational leadership teams in a fast-paced business environment.
Knowledge of ERP and Business Intelligence platforms, ideally SAP and related reporting tools.
Strong analytical and commercial acumen with a data-driven approach to decision-making.
Executive presence and perfect communication skills as this individual will be client-facing and regularly meet with Senior Leadership in Canada and at Head Office in Europe.
10+ years of experience including minimum 5 years as Controller.
CPA designation or MBA is required.

Leadership Competencies

Strategic, structured, and results-oriented leader.
High integrity with a strong ethical and professional approach.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
Strong business acumen with the ability to influence at executive level.
Resilient and adaptable, with the ability to manage complexity and change.
Passionate about developing people and building high-performing teams.
Collaborative, hands-on, and focused on delivering practical business outcomes.

What's on Offer

This is a unique opportunity to join a growing organization in a highly visible leadership role. You will have the chance to shape the financial direction of the business, influence strategic decisions, and lead a talented finance team while contributing to the company's long-term success and growth.

new_jobs.title: Director of Digital Marketing (Remote, Vancouver)
new_jobs.description:
Blacksmith Agency

Marketing
Full time
Remote (USA, Canada or South Africa)

About The Role

Blacksmith Agency runs PPC and SEO for clients across multifamily, B2B and technical verticals. As Director of Digital Marketing you lead that department. The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist report to you and they are the specialists in their channels. Right now nobody owns this function, which is the whole reason this seat is open.

This is a management seat, not a senior individual contributor one.
You will not be building campaigns, and on technical SEO your strategist will know more than you do. That is the arrangement, not a gap. You carry channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale. The strategists carry the execution of it, and you carry whether the department delivers.

What You Own

The PPC strategist and the SEO strategist: their quality bar, their development, their reviews, and the call when someone is not going to get there.
The standard the work is held to. What a good audit looks like, what gets checked before work leaves the agency, how an account is reported. You write it and you hold two specialists to it.
Client results across the whole function, including whether our reporting is honest. Nobody here is auditing attribution and GA4 accuracy today.
The escalation when an account is at risk. You diagnose it, you direct the strategist who fixes it, and you are on the call with the client.
Channel strategy and where budget goes as accounts scale.
What we tell sales we can credibly deliver, before it gets sold.
The hiring plan for the department, and first-round interviews for your own team, within about a quarter.

What You Need

Strategists or specialists who have reported to you, where their reviews, their development and the decision when someone was not working out were yours. Managing accounts is not this.
7+ years across paid media and SEO. Owning one channel while sitting beside the other does not count here.
Enough depth in Google Ads, GA4, Search Console, Meta and Microsoft Ads to tell good work from work that merely looks good. That is a lower bar than doing it and a higher bar than reading a report.
One account you turned around that you can talk through: the metric, the figure before, the figure after, and why the change worked. Whose hands were on the keyboard matters far less than whether the diagnosis was yours.
Comfortable being the client-facing owner when an account is underperforming. That call comes to you, not to the strategist.
Agency experience carrying many accounts at once.

Please do not apply if

Nobody has ever reported to you, or you have never owned someone's review or had to performance-manage anyone.
You have only ever run one channel.
All of your experience is in-house on a single brand.
What you actually want is to keep building campaigns yourself. That is not a lesser ambition, it is a different job, and this is not it.

None of these are preferences we bend on. They are how we screen, so applying anyway costs you an hour and gets you a no.

Process

Three conversations, then a decision. A thirty minute screen with our recruiter, a first round with the founder this seat reports to, and a final. No take-home project and no panel interview.

How To Apply

Four fields at the link, then a short 6 minute Predictive Index assessment. Use the same email throughout. No cover letter.
